project.project_title: Graphic Novel Script Adapter Needed — Create Polished Sample for Crowdfunding

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: I would like to proceed with the 12-page sample. If you want to accept, let me know and I will forward the contract. The terms will be those we discussed in our messages. Please ask if you have any questions; if not, I will send it shortly. Thanks!

value_updates.script_organization: each comic page laid out by panel

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hey [FREELANCER_NAME_001],
You have carte blanche on this. Because it is a sample piece, I will trust your judgement.
Tell me if you need anything from me.
[CLIENT_NAME_002]

value_updates.creative_discretion: The adapter has carte blanche and may exercise their own judgment.
permitted_adaptation_techniques: convert portions of scene descriptions into voice-over captions
omit brief exchanges to conserve page space and improve efficiency

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hello [FREELANCER_NAME_001]!
What would your total quote be for 80-85 pages?
Thanks!
[CLIENT_NAME_002]

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
I ran some calculations using the material I have already written.

First, can you confirm whether you mean 85 screenplay pages or 85 comic pages? My adaptation came out to an approximate 2:1 ratio of screenplay pages to comic pages.

If part 2 is roughly equal in length to episode 1, then parts 1 and 2 should amount to approximately 40-45 comic pages. I could quote $350 for that scope with a timeline of 2 weeks. If I can reuse 12 pages from the sample script, possibly with light revisions and page reflowing, I could reduce the price to $275.

I can also produce 80-85 comic pages, but that would probably require covering more of the story, presumably through episode 3 or 4. For that amount of work, I would suggest $675 with a 4-week turnaround, or $600 even if the 12 sample-script pages can be reused.

Please tell me which option is nearer to what you have in mind and whether these terms work for you.

Thanks,
[FREELANCER_NAME_001]

ambiguity.description: It is unresolved whether the requested length refers to screenplay pages or comic pages, which materially affects story coverage.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: The current projection is 85 pages of comic. Here are the next two scripts. I believe I also sent you a version of the novel, which is divided into three sections. That may serve as a better source than the scripts. Please review everything and tell me what you think.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
In that event, thank you very much. At that rate, I can devote additional time to determining the strongest presentation for all the material instead of adhering so closely to the screenplay.

Do you want me to begin next week, or should I wait until you explicitly tell me to "go?"

I can commit to writing 80-85 comic pages. I will review the next two episodes and the novel, then decide how much of the story can fit within that length. While planning it, should I pace the material with the expectation that I may eventually script the remainder of the story? In other words, should this portion feel self-contained, or should it be structured to leave readers wondering, "What's next?"

Thanks,
[FREELANCER_NAME_001]

ambiguity.description: It is unresolved whether the 80-85-page adaptation should feel self-contained or end in a continuation-oriented way.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: I am sorry for the misunderstanding. I am hoping to obtain funding, and the sample I paid for was part of that effort. If the campaign succeeds, I will proceed with the project. I am not requesting any work from you at this time. However, if you prefer to withdraw, please tell me ASAP.
